I worked hard last year to teach 21 periods a week, attend training sessions, further CPD sessions and gain my PGCE. I threw myself into research, and I still have a long way to go, and I’m prepared to continue putting work in to improve myself as a teacher.

Haven’t done much Twitter over the holidays. I have just walked into my flat after travelling halfway across the country with the heaviest bags but the lightest heart. This break has been wonderful ❤️

Last night my best friend asked me what my resolution was, and I drunkenly worded it as “to get a life”. I need to work smarter, not harder, to free up me time. I’ve joined a gym. I’m going to pick up a hobby. And I’m going to spend time with the people who mean most to me.

I often worry that I’m not getting my Y9s (1st year GCSE) to write enough practice essays... this has made me feel much better. I’m not shoe-horning them in to tick a box, they’ll write them when they’re more comfortable with the content we have covered
Interesting is one way of putting it. Actually looking forward to reading their assessments sat today and seeing what they’ve got for me! This is when marking can get (dare I say it) fun!
Been sat in a coffee shop since midday marking KS4 assessments. Have to do this so I’m not distracted at home. If I wasn’t marking I’d be planning. Every Sunday.

Keeping my work week manageable by working *most* Sunday’s. Today, KS4 assessments so that when I get my KS5 ones back this week I can do them on time, and get them done in time for yet more Y11 mocks (that’s a separate issue)
Amazing what focussing in the writing skills for my Y12s has done. thanks for the recent blog posts, they have helped my students (and myself!) improve so much!
Pros/Cons is being a GCSE examiner? This hear they’re inviting NQTs and I have mixed feelings about it... #historyteacher #Edexcel

In September I start a new job - as sole history teacher for a brand new school. While I’m going to enjoy teaching and developing a curriculum just for Year 7... my Year 11s made my heart happy yesterday in our last ‘official’ lesson. New beginnings though 😀
I’m telling them, hopefully tomorrow I’ll get them inside Clifford’s Tower or the Gates for the War of the Roses stuff!!

Have spent the majority of the half term enjoying the sun, spending time with family and binge-watching Outlander on Amazon Prime... and genuinely feel quite content. Having that “back to school” feeling now though - last minute revision session for Year 11 tomorrow (NOT my idea)
Quite emotional sending my first ever lot of Y11s off to their final exam... they've been a lovely bunch to teach, definitely my favourite class despite the constant chatter. Will be missing them!
Laying a wreath and a cross at the Menin Gate and Lijssenthoek on the grave of Staff Nurse Nellie Spindler, one of only two women killed in WWI to be buried in Belgium #harrisbattlefields
Looking far too happy at being in a trench. Fascinating place, big love for the Memorial Museum at Passchendaele! #ww1centenary #Passchendaele #historyteacher

Top: Sunken Lane, 1st Battalion Lancashire Fusilliers, the morning of 1st July, 1916, ready for their 7:30 attack at the BAttle of the Somme. Bottom: students, 102 years later, 24th June 2018, in commemoration #harrisbattlefields #somme #ww1

This morning was spent mostly at Tyne Cot ceremony. Students, having researched war dead linked to their own school community, were able to commemorate them in their final resting place. “Age does not determine bravery...” #harrisbattlefields #ww1

Sat crying in my classroom at a letter from a Year 11 student. She’s proud of her legacy of being the only student I gave a warning to in the two years I taught her class, and roasted me for my terrible history memes. I’ll miss this lot #goodbyes #year11

Despite what the numbers say tomorrow, I’m so proud of my students. We’ve spent the past two years trying our damned hardest, and each one of them tried their best (or so they swore to me on their way out of all three papers)! That’s all we can ask for! #GCSEresultsday
